Offset(*source: Ids*, */*, *d: float \| tuple\[float, Point\]*, *both_sides: bool \| None = None*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")  
Add new elements at distance d from source that follow it: the exact offset, round around corners, sharp where the sides cross.

The offset of a spline is a curve at exactly d (kind ‘Spline’). With the constraints on, the offset follows the source and ‘\<id\>.d’; a change of d moves the geometry as little as it can, a free source too: fix or dimension the source to keep it. A QuickSketch makes the same elements without ties, a spline’s offset as an ordinary spline within config.spline_tol. The pens stay (a Rectangle after it follows the pen’s direction; dir= sets it). A source cannot be removed while the offset exists (sk(‘Line.2’).construction = True keeps it); the offset’s parts cannot be removed, trimmed, split, fixed or copied alone.

Parameters:  
- **source** – an id, a wire id or a list of ids forming one chain of lines, arcs and splines; or one circle or closed spline.

- **d** – the distance. A closed chain gets one loop, outside for d \> 0, inside for d \< 0; an open chain both sides with round caps (‘\<id\>.startcap’, ‘\<id\>.endcap’). (d, point): the side the point ((h, v) or a point id) lies on, d \> 0.

- **both_sides** – True both sides (a closed chain: both loops); False one side (an open chain: the left for d \> 0, the right for d \< 0, no caps); default one side for a closed chain, both for an open one.

- **options** – id= the offset’s id, default ‘Offset.N’. One side: ‘\<id\>.Line.3’ is the offset of Line.3, ‘\<id\>.Line.3.corner’ the round corner around the end of Line.3. Both sides: the side word first, ‘\<id\>.left.Line.3’, ‘\<id\>.right.Line.3.corner’, and ‘\<id\>.left’, ‘\<id\>.right’ the sides (a loop counts counterclockwise: left is its inside). ‘\<id\>’ is all of it; ‘\<id\>.d’ its distance, a dimension. name=, maxh=, minh=, hpref=, layer=, col=, partition=, construction=: the elements’ properties, by default those of the source.

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – d = 0; a source that is not one chain; d at or beyond the radius of a spline’s tightest bend towards the side (a cusp). Later, a change of d or of the source that needs another shape (an arc’s offset vanishing or coming back, a corner appearing, a cusp, sides crossing) raises and changes nothing: Remove(‘\<id\>’), then Offset again.

- **TypeError** – d is neither a distance nor (d, point), or an unknown keyword.

Examples

``` python
sk.Offset('plate', -2, id='wall')
sk.Offset('s', (1.5, (10, 40)), id='bead')
```

Plot(*ax: Any = None*, *show_constraints: bool \| None = None*, *show_ends: bool = False*, *show_direction: bool = False*, *show_parent: Any = None*, *backend: str \| None = None*) → Any  
Draws the sketch with matplotlib or plotly, every element in the colour of its state.

Green is fully constrained, black free, pink over-constrained (a constraint that contradicts the others and the elements it contradicts; all free while the constraints are disabled); construction elements are dashed, projected elements gold; in plotly an element shows its id when hovered. The signs, pieces and arrows keep their size on screen when zooming.

Parameters:  
- **ax** – a matplotlib Axes or a plotly Figure to draw into, which also selects the backend.

- **show_constraints** – True adds a sign per constraint (in plotly what it is when hovered; not while the constraints are disabled); a QuickSketch has none and warns.

- **show_ends** – True adds a blue start and an orange end piece on every line and arc.

- **show_direction** – True adds an arrow from start to end on every line and arc.

- **show_parent** – an OCC solid (e.g. the one whose face the sketch lies on) drawn projected into the sketch’s plane under the sketch, its faces lightly filled, its edges black (in plotly with their names when hovered); only in the plot.

- **backend** – “matplotlib” or “plotly” (hover) without ax; None is matplotlib.

Returns:  
the matplotlib Axes or the plotly Figure.

Raises:  
**ValueError** – backend is unknown.

Examples

``` python
sk.Plot(show_constraints=True)
sk.Plot(show_parent=box, backend="plotly")
```

Draws planex objects, planes and OCC shapes in one 3d view.

Rectangle(*l: float*, *w: float*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")\
Rectangle(*p0: Point*, *p1: Point*, */*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")\
Rectangle(*p0: Point*, *p1: Point*, *p2: Point*, */*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")  
Draw a rectangle from the pen, l along the drawing direction and w to its left, or through its corners.

Its four lines are Rectangle.k.Line.1 to .Line.4 from the start corner along the drawing direction (counterclockwise), and Rectangle.k is their wire (sk(‘Rectangle.1’), Offset(‘Rectangle.1’, 2), Remove, the patterns). It is not part of a chain; its three right angles are Rectangle.k.Perpendicular.1 to .3; the pen stays at the start corner.

Through corners: two opposite corners p0, p1 (in any order) give a rectangle with its sides along h and v, starting at the corner of the smallest h and v (in a px.Sketch its first side is also Horizontal). Three points: p0 to p1 is a side and the opposite side runs through p2, which sets the width; it starts at p0 and runs counterclockwise (with p2 to the right of p0 -\> p1, Line.1 leaves p0 along its other side and Line.4 runs p1 -\> p0). A corner is a point (h, v) or a selected point such as sk(‘A’), which it is tied to (p2: the opposite side passes through it). The pen stays where it was.

Parameters:  
- **l** – the length along the drawing direction.

- **w** – the width to the left of it.

- **p0** – a corner.

- **p1** – the opposite corner (two points), or the corner after p0 (three points).

- **p2** – a point on the side opposite p0 -\> p1.

- **options** – id= replaces Rectangle.k (id=’plate’ gives plate.Line.1 to plate.Line.4 and the wire ‘plate’); the lines’ properties name=, maxh=, minh=, hpref=, layer=, col=, partition=, construction=.

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – id is taken or no valid id, a side within rounding of 0, a selection of more than one point.

- **TypeError** – id_wire= (the id names the wire), an unknown keyword, a corner that is no point or an id string, or four points.

Examples

``` python
sk.Rectangle(40, 20, id='plate', maxh=2)
sk.Rectangle((0, 0), (40, 20))
```

RectangleC(*l: float*, *w: float*, */*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")\
RectangleC(*center: Point*, *l: float*, *w: float*, */*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")  
Draw a rectangle centred at the pen or at center, l along the drawing direction and w across it.

Its four lines are RectangleC.k.Line.1 to .Line.4 from the corner behind and to the right of the centre, along the drawing direction (counterclockwise), and RectangleC.k is their wire. The construction line RectangleC.k.diagonal runs from the first corner to the third, the construction point RectangleC.k.center sits at its middle; a selected point as center ties the centre to it. It is not part of a chain; the pen goes to the centre and keeps its direction.

Parameters:  
- **center** – the centre: a point (h, v) or a selected point such as sk(‘A’) (tied to it); default the pen.

- **l** – the length along the drawing direction.

- **w** – the width across it.

- **options** – id= replaces RectangleC.k (id=’plate’ gives plate.Line.1 to plate.Line.4, plate.center and the wire ‘plate’); the lines’ properties name=, maxh=, minh=, hpref=, layer=, col=, partition=, construction=.

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – a side within rounding of 0, a selection of more than one point, id is taken or no valid id.

- **TypeError** – l or w is no number, center is an id string or no point, id_wire= or an unknown keyword.

Examples

``` python
sk.RectangleC(40, 20)
sk.RectangleC((10, 5), 40, 20, id='plate')
```

Slot(*l: float*, *w: float*, */*, *\*flags: [Constraint](#planex.Constraint "planex.Constraint")*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")\
Slot(*dh: float*, *dv: float*, *w: float*, */*, *\*flags: [Constraint](#planex.Constraint "planex.Constraint")*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")\
Slot(*to: Point \| Id*, *w: float*, */*, *\*flags: [Constraint](#planex.Constraint "planex.Constraint")*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")\
Slot(*from\_: Point \| Id*, *to: Point \| Id*, *w: float*, */*, *\*flags: [Constraint](#planex.Constraint "planex.Constraint")*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")\
Slot(*\*ends: Point \| Id \| float \| [Constraint](#planex.Constraint "planex.Constraint")*, *until: Id \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| SketchUntil \| None = None*, *parallel: Id \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| None = None*, *perpendicular: Id \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| None = None*, *angle: float \| tuple\[float, Id\] \| None = None*, *congruent: Id \| None = None*, *tangent: Id \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| tuple\[Id, Id\] \| None = None*, *distance: float \| tuple\[float, Point\] \| None = None*, *through: Point \| None = None*, *reverse: bool = False*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")  
Draw a straight slot: a line and its offset on both sides, closed by round caps.

Every form of Line, with the width w as the last number before the flags. The line is the slot’s spine, a construction element; the outline is its offset at w / 2 on both sides, the caps half circles around the spine’s ends. The pen goes on at the spine’s end in its direction (a new chain). Slot.k is the wire of the outline, with Slot.k.spine, Slot.k.left and Slot.k.right (left and right of the spine’s direction), Slot.k.startcap and Slot.k.endcap. A Sketch keeps the slot a slot when the spine moves, and has the dimension Slot.k.w (sk\[“Slot.1.w”\] = 6; sk.Update()); with auto_constraint the spine gets what Line gets. Remove(“Slot.1”) removes the whole slot.

Parameters:  
- **w** – the width of the slot, across the spine; positive.

- **l** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **dh** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **dv** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **to** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **from** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **ends** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **flags** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **until** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **parallel** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **perpendicular** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **angle** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **congruent** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **tangent** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **distance** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **through** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **reverse** – as for Line, which draws the spine.

- **options** – id= replaces Slot.k (id=’groove’ gives groove.spine, groove.left, …), and the outline’s properties name=, maxh=, minh=, hpref=, layer=, col=, partition=, construction=.

Raises:  
- **TypeError** – no width as the last number, another form of arguments, an unknown keyword.

- **ValueError** – w is not positive; the spine has no length or cannot be placed; id is taken.

Examples

``` python
sk.Slot(10, 4)
sk.Slot((0, 0), (0, 10), 2, id="groove")
```

Spline(*points: list\[tuple\[float, float\]\]*, */*, *\*flags: [Constraint](#planex.Constraint "planex.Constraint")*, *periodic: bool = False*, *tangents: dict\[int, tuple\[float, float\]\] \| None = None*, *start_from_localpos: bool = True*, *style: str \| None = None*, *tol: float \| None = None*, *\*\*options*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")  
Draw a spline from the pen’s position through points; its points are point elements.

Parameters:  
- **points** – the points (h, v) it passes, after the start.

- **flags** – px.Fix; px.Tangent (with the element before it).

- **periodic** – closed back to its start.

- **tangents** – {index: (dh, dv)}, directions at some of the points, index 0 the start; they become angle unknowns.

- **start_from_localpos** – False starts at the first point instead of the pen’s position.

- **style** – ‘px’ (planex’s: closed without tangents the C2 periodic cubic) or ‘occ’ (OCC’s Geom2dAPI_Interpolate, netgen’s splines; a sketch keeps tangent directions only, so two points with one tangent of another length than 1 differ from netgen’s); default config.spline_style.

- **tol** – ignored.

- **options** – id= (the spline’s id), and its properties name=, maxh=, minh=, hpref=, layer=, col=, partition=, construction=.

Examples

``` python
sk.Spline([(5, 2), (10, 0)])
sk.Spline([(5, 2), (10, 0), (5, -2)], periodic=True, tangents={0: (0, 1)})
```

Split(*a: Id*, *b: Ids \| None = None*, */*, *\**, *auto_constraint: bool = True*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")  
Cut a into pieces where it meets b.

The pieces are ‘Line.3.1’, ‘Line.3.2’, … along it (a circle’s from the piece at 0 degrees, counterclockwise), and ‘Line.3’ is the wire of the pieces, which what referred to Line.3 (its ends, its length, a tangency) resolves through. The cut points stay on b.

Parameters:  
- **a** – the element.

- **b** – what cuts it: an id, a list or a selection; default every other line, arc and circle.

- **auto_constraint** – keep the pieces on one line or circle; False lets them move apart (an arc’s pieces get their own centres and radii).

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – a given as (a, point): every piece is numbered, none keeps a’s id.

- **TypeError** – a keyword other than auto_constraint.

Examples

``` python
sk.Split("Line.3", "Line.5")
sk.Split("Circle.1", ["Line.1", "Line.2"], auto_constraint=False)
```

SymmetryLine(*a: Point \| Id*, *b: Point \| Id*, */*, *\**, *reverse: bool = False*, *id: str \| None = None*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")  
Add the infinite construction line that mirrors a onto b.

Crossing lines: the bisector mapping a onto b best; parallel lines: the midline; points: their perpendicular bisector; circles and arcs: that of the centres, whatever radii drawn. The line is free to move and kept there by symmetry constraints: on the lines’ carriers (never equal lengths), the points, or the centres of the circles or arcs (with equal radii, never their ends).

Parameters:  
- **a** – a line, point, circle or arc.

- **b** – one of the same kind.

- **reverse** – of two crossing lines the other bisector.

- **id** – the line’s id, default SymmetryLine.N.

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – a and b are not two points, two lines or two circles, or two circles or arcs share their centre.

- **TypeError** – an unknown keyword.

Examples

``` python
sk.SymmetryLine("Line.1", "Line.3")
sk.SymmetryLine("Circle.1", "Circle.2", id="mid")
```

ToOCCFace(*fit_splines: bool \| dict \| None = None*, *remove_edges_smaller: float \| None = None*, *close_gaps_smaller: float \| None = None*, *remove_free_edges: bool \| None = None*, *merge_collinear_closer: float \| None = None*, *remove_faces_smaller: float \| None = None*, *merge_small_faces_instead: bool \| None = None*, *fit_arcs: bool \| dict \| None = None*) → occ.Face \| occ.Compound  
The region of the drawn elements as an OCC face, a compound of faces if it has several parts, made from a cleaned copy.

Parameters:  
- **fit_splines** – fits splines to chains of short edges: True, False or a dict of the fit’s options (tol, max_edge_length, max_edge_angle, ignore_edges_smaller); None takes px.config.fit_splines.

- **remove_edges_smaller** – removes lines and arcs no longer than this; None takes px.config.remove_edges_smaller.

- **close_gaps_smaller** – closes gaps between ends up to this; None takes px.config.close_gaps_smaller.

- **remove_free_edges** – removes the edges that touch no other edge at either end; None takes px.config.remove_free_edges, False for a wire export. In a Shape only the edges of its faces go, its wires stay (a wire of one isolated edge too).

- **merge_collinear_closer** – merges two lines whose common vertex is this close to the line through their far ends; None takes px.config.merge_collinear_closer.

- **remove_faces_smaller** – removes the faces of less area than this (0: none); None takes px.config.remove_faces_smaller.

- **merge_small_faces_instead** – True unites such a face with the face it shares the longest boundary with instead; None takes px.config.merge_small_faces_instead.

- **fit_arcs** – fits arcs to chains of short edges: True, False or a dict of FitArcs’ options; None takes px.config.fit_arcs.

Raises:  
**ValueError** – in mode=’strict’ while the sketch can still move.

Examples

``` python
sk.ToOCCFace()
sk.ToOCCFace(fit_arcs=True)
```

ToSVG(*size: float = 300*, *\*\*options: Any*) → str \| None  
The object as the text of an SVG picture in its plane coordinates, its faces filled.

A sketch is drawn in its own look: every element in the colour of its state (green fully constrained, black free, pink over-constrained) with its id when hovered, construction dashed, in a frame with numbered ticks on a grid.

Parameters:  
- **obj** – a Face, Shape, Wire, Compound, sketch or DeformableShape.

- **size** – the larger side of the picture in pixels.

- **options** – for a sketch: show_constraints=True adds a sign per constraint, show_ends=True a blue start and an orange end piece on every line and arc, show_direction=True an arrow from start to end; other objects ignore them.

Returns:  
the SVG text; None if the object has no extent.

Examples

``` python
face.ToSVG()
sk.ToSVG(size=500, show_constraints=True)
```

ToShapely(*tol: float = 0.001*) → Any  
Converts to a shapely geometry in plane coordinates, arcs and splines sampled within tol.

Faces that share an edge (a glued Shape) give a GeometryCollection of their polygons, since a MultiPolygon must not have parts sharing an edge.

Parameters:  
- **obj** – the Face, Shape, Wire, sketch (its Shape()) or Compound.

- **tol** – the largest distance of a chord from its arc or spline, a length. Where a face is thinner than tol its polygon is sampled again finer (to tol/1000), with a warning; still invalid, it is made valid (make_valid).

Returns:  
a Polygon or MultiPolygon for a Face, a Shape of faces or a sketch; a LineString or MultiLineString for a Wire or a Shape of wires; a GeometryCollection for a Compound or a Shape of both.

Examples

``` python
face.ToShapely()
px.ToShapely(shape, tol=1e-4)
```

Trim(*a: Id \| tuple\[Id, Point\]*, *b: Ids \| None = None*, */*, *\**, *reverse: bool = False*) → [Sketch](#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch")  
Cut a where it meets b and make one piece of it a construction element (‘Line.3.trimmed.1’).

The cut points stay on b. One piece left keeps a’s id; a cut out of the middle leaves ‘Line.3.1’, ‘Line.3.2’, and ‘Line.3’ is the wire of the pieces, which what referred to Line.3 resolves through. Without b and with nothing to cut at, all of a becomes construction.

Parameters:  
- **a** – the element; (id, point) picks the piece nearest the point ((h, v) or a point id), else the piece nearest the pen is trimmed.

- **b** – what cuts it: an id, a list or a selection; default every other line, arc and circle, construction ones included (RectangleC’s diagonal cuts a line through the rectangle’s center).

- **reverse** – trim the next nearest piece.

Raises:  
- **TypeError** – a keyword other than reverse (near=: the point goes with a).

- **ValueError** – a names a wire or group, not one element.

Examples

``` python
sk.Trim("Line.3", "Line.5")
sk.Trim(("Line.3", (4, 0)), "Line.5", reverse=True)
```

Wire(*unify: bool = True*, *\**, *id: str \| None = None*) → [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire")  
The drawn edges as one Wire, its ends within rounding joined; construction elements take no part.

Parameters:  
- **unify** – True cuts the drawn edges at crossings and T-junctions, keeps an overlapping stretch once and merges the pieces on one carrier where nothing else meets (as wire + wire); False keeps every drawn element uncut.

Raises:

Wires(*unify: bool = True*, *\**, *id: str \| None = None*) → list\[[Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire")\]  
The drawn edges as a list of Wire, each one chain in traversal order; ends within rounding are joined, a larger gap stays open; construction elements take no part.

Parameters:  
- **unify** – True (as px.Wires) cuts the drawn edges at crossings and T-junctions, keeps an overlapping stretch once and merges the pieces on one carrier where nothing else meets: an outline with a rib ending on it is one closed wire and the rib its own. False keeps every drawn element uncut (an overlap stays twice) and joins them at their ends.

- **id** – the id of what it returns (of a list’s items id.1, id.2, …, of a dict’s id.key); default the kind that made it and a number, given when first asked for.

Raises:  
**ValueError** – with unify=False a chain crosses, touches or overlaps itself (the message names the two elements); in mode=’strict’ while the sketch can still move.

Examples

``` python

sk.Wires(unify=False)
```

WriteGeo(*path: str \| os.PathLike*, */*) → None  
Writes the edges and faces as a gmsh .geo file.

Points carry the maxh of their edges and faces as the characteristic length; lines, circle arcs (split at half a circle) and splines as B-splines through planex’s approximation (not exact: .geo has no NURBS), every curve once; plane surfaces with their holes. Physical groups: a curve group per edge name, a surface group per face name, the unnamed edges and faces in a curve and a surface group named “unnamed” (gmsh writes only elements in a group once there is one, and netgen’s ReadGmsh needs every group named and the boundary segments). Periodic identifications become Periodic Curve.

Parameters:  
- **obj** – the Face, Shape, Wire, sketch or Compound to write.

- **path** – the file to write.

Examples

``` python
face.WriteGeo("part.geo")
px.WriteGeo(shape, "part.geo")
```

*property* error_on_branch_change  
bool

Whether a solve that turns a line round or an arc to its other side (it leaves the branch the sketch was drawn in, even in the smallest steps Update takes) is an error that changes nothing, else a warning; on by default in mode=’strict’.

Type:  
error_on_branch_change

dict\[str, str\]

The expressions, {id: the text as given}.

Type:  
expressions

*property* id  
str

The object’s id: the kind that made it and a number, given when first asked for (Sketch.1, Shape.3), or set (an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, \_ and single inner spaces); its elements’ ids follow it (Shape.3.Line.2).

Type:  
id

*property* jacobian  
dict

The solver’s Jacobian at the geometry now, as a dict.

‘matrix’: the derivatives of the residuals (rows) with respect to the solver’s scaled unknowns (columns), a scipy.sparse.csr_array when scipy is installed, else its arrays (data, indices, indptr), as scipy.sparse.csr_array((data, indices, indptr), shape=shape) takes them. ‘shape’: (rows, columns). ‘rows’: per row (constraint id, row in it); an arc’s own equations (arc id, row); the equation that holds a dimension an expression uses (dimension id, ‘value’). ‘columns’: per unknown (reference, coordinate), as (‘Line.1.end’, ‘x’), (‘Circle.1’, ‘r’), (‘Spline.1.p2’, ‘angle’), a linked dimension’s (‘w’, ‘value’) or a constraint’s own (‘RigidGroup.1’, ‘param 0’). ‘scale’: per column the unknown per scaled unknown: 1 for a length, 180 / (pi x the size of the sketch) for an angle (in degrees); matrix\[:, k\] / scale\[k\] is the derivative per unit (per degree) of unknown k. ‘row_scale’: per row the change of its residual per unit of its value: 1 for a length dimension and a row without a value; per degree for an angle dimension: its lever (the shortest element it relates) x pi/180, the size of the sketch x pi/180 on the ‘value’ row of a linked one or on a pattern’s angle.

The change of every unknown per unit (per degree) of the dimension in row i is scale \* spsolve(matrix, row_scale\[i\] \* e_i).

Reading it raises ValueError while the constraints are disabled.

How far every unknown moves per degree of the dimension phi, with scipy:

> from scipy.sparse.linalg import spsolve J = sk.jacobian i = J\[‘rows’\].index((‘phi’, 0)) e = np.zeros(J\[‘shape’\]\[0\]) e\[i\] = J\[‘row_scale’\]\[i\] per_degree = dict(zip(J\[‘columns’\], J\[‘scale’\] \* spsolve(J\[‘matrix’\].tocsc(), e))) per_degree\[(‘crank.end’, ‘x’)\] \# how far crank.end moves in x per degree of phi

Type:  
jacobian

*property* locations  
dict\[str, tuple\[float, float\]\]

Every point reference with where it is, solved, {ref: (h, v)}.

Type:  
locations

*property* measures  
dict

The standard measurements and the stored ones, evaluated now, as a dict.

Type:  
measures

*property* mode  
str

The mode, ‘normal’ or ‘strict’: setting ‘strict’ also switches error_on_branch_change on (not while the constraints are disabled).

Type:  
mode

Type:

Type:

*property* points

Type:

# Boolean operations and transformations

Operations on lists of parts and the transformations. The operators `+`, `-` and `*` and the methods of the objects are listed with their classes. See [Boolean operations](../core/booleans/index.md) for the guide.

Unify(*parts: list\[[Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [Compound](geometry.md#planex.Compound "planex.Compound")\]*, */*, *multithreaded: bool = True*, *\**, *id: str \| None = None*) → [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape")  
The union of all faces and shapes, or of all wires (their connected chains), as a balanced tree of pairwise unions.

A region has the properties of the faces it holds, merged in list order; compounds give their parts.

Parameters:  
- **parts** – faces, shapes, wires and compounds.

- **multithreaded** – True runs the pairwise unions in parallel.

- **id** – the id of what it returns (of a list’s items id.1, id.2, …, of a dict’s id.key); default the kind that made it and a number, given when first asked for.

Raises:  
**TypeError** – an item is not a Face, Shape, Wire or Compound.

Examples

``` python
px.Unify([a, b, c])
px.Unify(parts, multithreaded=False)
```

&nbsp;

Subtract(*parts: list\[[Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire")\]*, */*, *multithreaded: bool = True*, *\**, *id: str \| None = None*) → [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape")  
The first part minus the union of all others; every region keeps the properties of the first one’s face.

Parameters:  
- **parts** – faces, shapes and wires, the first the one subtracted from.

- **multithreaded** – True runs the pairwise operations in parallel.

- **id** – the id of what it returns (of a list’s items id.1, id.2, …, of a dict’s id.key); default the kind that made it and a number, given when first asked for.

Raises:  
**TypeError** – an item is not a Face, Shape or Wire (a Compound: px.Unify merges it first).

Examples

``` python

```

Intersect(*parts: list\[[Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire")\]*, */*, *multithreaded: bool = True*, *\**, *id: str \| None = None*) → [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape")  
The intersection of all faces and shapes, as a balanced tree of pairwise intersections.

Every region keeps the first one’s properties, maxh and minh the smallest of the faces it lies in.

Parameters:  
- **parts** – faces, shapes and wires.

- **multithreaded** – True runs the pairwise intersections in parallel.

- **id** – the id of what it returns (of a list’s items id.1, id.2, …, of a dict’s id.key); default the kind that made it and a number, given when first asked for.

Raises:  
**TypeError** – an item is not a Face, Shape or Wire (a Compound: px.Unify merges it first).

Examples

``` python

```

&nbsp;

Glue(*parts: list\[[Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [Compound](geometry.md#planex.Compound "planex.Compound")\]*, */*, *\**, *id: str \| None = None*) → [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape")  
The parts as one shape, as netgen’s occ.Glue: everything cut against everything, every area covered by a different set of faces a face of its own (A - B, A \* B, B - A).

The faces’ properties merge in list order, the first winning an overlap; a part lying entirely inside another keeps its own region and properties; touching faces share their edge; a wire through a face splits it into two faces with its properties, a wire piece inside a face that separates nothing stays an internal edge of it (the mesh follows it). Where parts share an edge their edge properties merge the same way.

Parameters:  
- **parts** – faces, shapes, wires and compounds (their contents).

- **id** – the id of what it returns (of a list’s items id.1, id.2, …, of a dict’s id.key); default the kind that made it and a number, given when first asked for.

Raises:  
**TypeError** – an item is not a Face, Shape, Wire or Compound.

Examples

``` python
px.Glue([air, iron])
px.Glue([plate, px.Line((1, -1), (1, 3))])
```


&nbsp;

GetTransformation(*a: [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [EdgeView](selections.md#planex.EdgeView "planex.EdgeView") \| [EdgesView](selections.md#planex.EdgesView "planex.EdgesView") \| [Selection](selections.md#planex.Selection "planex.Selection") \| [LineEdge](geometry.md#planex.LineEdge "planex.LineEdge") \| [ArcEdge](geometry.md#planex.ArcEdge "planex.ArcEdge") \| list*, *b: [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [EdgeView](selections.md#planex.EdgeView "planex.EdgeView") \| [EdgesView](selections.md#planex.EdgesView "planex.EdgesView") \| [Selection](selections.md#planex.Selection "planex.Selection") \| [LineEdge](geometry.md#planex.LineEdge "planex.LineEdge") \| [ArcEdge](geometry.md#planex.ArcEdge "planex.ArcEdge") \| list*, */*, *reverse: bool = False*) → Transformation  
The map of the plane taking the chain of lines and arcs a onto b, vertex onto vertex.

A straight chain, a single arc or a circle maps by a similarity (turn, uniform scale, move), other chains by the affine map of the vertices; every vertex and edge midpoint must land. Of the possible pairings it takes the one closest to a translation (orientation kept, the smallest turn).

Parameters:  
- **a** – the edges mapped: a wire, face, shape, edge view, edges view, selection, LineEdge, ArcEdge, or a list of them.

- **b** – the edges a lands on, in the same forms.

- **reverse** – True takes the best pairing running the other way.

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – a or b has no edges, has a spline, branches or is not one connected chain; they have different numbers of vertices; no map takes a onto b.

- **TypeError** – a or b has no edges to take.

Examples

``` python
px.GetTransformation(face.edges[0], face.edges[2])
px.GetTransformation(left, right, reverse=True)
```

---

Source: https://planex2d.org/docs/api/selections.md

# Selections and views

The edges, faces and vertices of an object are views: a property set on a view changes the object. See [Measuring](../core/measuring/index.md) for queries and selections in use.

Find(*id: str*) → Any  
The object with this id, or the elements the rest of the id names in it.

Only ids already given are found: an auto id is given when it is first asked for, a sketch’s when it is made. A part of a compound is named by the compound’s id, then the part’s (“both.plate”, “both.plate.Line.2”); a plain id names the object outside any compound, else the one part that has it.

Parameters:  
**id** – the id: an object’s (“Sketch.1”), or an object’s and an element’s in it (“Sketch.1.Line.5”).

Returns:  
the object, or a Selection of the elements.

Raises:  
**ValueError** – no object has the id, several objects have it, or the rest names no element.

Examples

``` python
px.Find("Sketch.1")
px.Find("both.plate.Line.2")
```

&nbsp;

*class* Selection(*items: Any*, */*)  
Elements of an object, chosen: edges, faces, vertices, sketch elements and points.

obj(…), obj.edges(…), obj.faces(…), obj.vertices(…) and sk(…) make one; calling it chooses further (see \_\_call\_\_); \[\] takes an index, a slice, a list of indices or a condition (px.x \> 5, combined with & \| ~). Setting a property (name, maxh, col, …) sets it on every element; reading it gives the value they share, None if they differ.

Parameters:  
**items** – the elements.

Examples

``` python
shape.edges(name="web")(kind="arc")
shape.edges[(px.x > 5) & (px.h < 2)].Min("length")
```

Copy() → [Compound](geometry.md#planex.Compound "planex.Compound")  
Copies of everything selected as one Compound; the object they were selected from stays as it is.

Faces become Faces, edges Wires with their properties, sketch elements their Wires.

Raises:  
**TypeError** – a vertex or point is selected (\[v.Copy() for v in selection\] copies vertices).

Examples

``` python
shape.edges(name="slot").Copy()
```

Distance(*target: Point \| Point3 \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [EdgeView](#planex.EdgeView "planex.EdgeView") \| [VertexView](#planex.VertexView "planex.VertexView") \| [FaceView](#planex.FaceView "planex.FaceView") \| TopoDS_Shape \| np.ndarray*, */*, *project: bool = False*, *components: str \| None = None*, *on_carrier: bool = False*, *signed: bool = False*) → float \| tuple\[float, ...\] \| np.ndarray  
The smallest distance from the edge to the target, or from the whole line or circle it lies on.

A target in another plane is measured in 3d, or projected into this plane with project.

Parameters:  
- **target** – a point, (h, v) in the plane or (x, y, z) in 3d, a Face, Shape, Wire, edge, vertex, face of a shape or OCC shape; many points as an (n, 2) or (n, 3) array.

- **project** – True projects a target in another plane into this one.

- **components** – letters of ‘hvxyz’: the components of the shortest connection from here to the target instead of its length.

- **on_carrier** – True measures to the whole line or circle the edge lies on.

- **signed** – only False: an edge has no inside.

Returns:  
a float; with components a tuple of them, one letter a float; many points an array (n,), with k components (n, k), one letter (n,).

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – signed=True; components has other letters; on_carrier for a spline, or with a target off the plane without project.

- **TypeError** – the target has another form.

Examples

``` python
edge.Distance((5, 0))
edge.Distance((5, 3), on_carrier=True)
```

Measure(*to: Point \| Point3 \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [EdgeView](#planex.EdgeView "planex.EdgeView") \| None = None*, *project: bool = False*) → dict\
Measure(*f: Callable*, */*, *\*args*, *id: str \| None = None*, *\*\*params*) → object  
The measures of the edge as a dict, with the keys of Wire.Measure.

Parameters:  
- **to** – anything Distance takes: adds the distance to it.

- **project** – True projects a target of to in another plane into this one.

- **f** – a measurement, a callable f(obj, \*args, \*\*params) (see px.measurements): Measure returns its value.

- **args** – the further arguments of f.

- **params** – the keyword arguments of f.

Raises:

Mirrored(*point: Point*, */*, *dir: tuple\[float, float\]*, *\**, *id: str \| None = None*) → [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire")\
Mirrored(*point: Point3*, */*, *normal: tuple\[float, float, float\]*, *\**, *id: str \| None = None*) → [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire")  
The edge as a Wire of its own, mirrored at the line through point along dir in its plane, or at the plane through point with normal in 3d; the edge is not changed.

In 3d its plane is mirrored and keeps a right-handed coordinate system, so its coordinates in the plane are mirrored at the plane’s first axis.

Parameters:  
- **point** – a point of the mirror line, (h, v), or of the mirror plane in 3d, (x, y, z).

- **dir** – the direction of the mirror line in the plane, (dh, dv).

- **normal** – the normal of the mirror plane in 3d, (dx, dy, dz).

- **id** – the id of what it returns (of a list’s items id.1, id.2, …, of a dict’s id.key); default the kind that made it and a number, given when first asked for.

Raises:  
**ValueError** – a value is not finite.

Examples

``` python
edge.Mirrored((0, 0), (0, 1))
edge.Mirrored((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0))
```

*class* FaceView  
A face of a shape, a px.Face for isinstance: its properties, edges and vertices are the shape’s, a change is made there; what only reads works on Copy(). It holds while the shape’s edges are unchanged.

Chamfer(*\*args*, *\*\*kwargs*)  
Refused: a face of a shape is not changed alone; Copy().Chamfer(…) changes a copy.

Parameters:

- **kwargs** – its keyword arguments.

Chamfered(*at: [VertexView](#planex.VertexView "planex.VertexView") \| Point \| str \| list\[[VertexView](#planex.VertexView "planex.VertexView") \| Point \| str\]*, *d: float*, */*, *d2: float \| None = None*, *angle: float \| None = None*, *reverse: bool = False*) → [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face")  
A copy with the corners chamfered as Chamfer does; this Face is not changed.

Parameters:  
- **at** – the corners: a vertex (face.vertices\[0\]), a point (h, v) on a vertex, a vertex name (every vertex with that name), or a list or selection of these; there is no default.

- **d** – the length on the first edge, a length \> 0; also on the second if d2 and angle are None.

- **d2** – the length on the second edge, a length \> 0; None: not given.

- **angle** – with d, the angle in degrees between the chamfer and the first edge, measured at its cut point towards the corner, between 0 and 180; None: not given. d2 and angle exclude each other.

- **reverse** – True makes the second edge the first.

Returns:  
the copy.

Raises:  
- **TypeError** – at is none of the forms above.

- **ValueError** – a size is not positive and finite, the angle is not between 0 and 180 or d2 and angle are both given, no corner is given, a name is no vertex’s name, a vertex belongs to another object, or no corner can be cut (the message names each corner and why); nothing changes then.

Examples

``` python
face.Chamfered((4, 0), 1)
face.Chamfered([(4, 0), (4, 4)], 1, d2=2)
```

CloseGaps(*tol: float*) → [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face")  
Joins every endpoint without an exact match on another edge with all endpoints of other edges within tol, in place.

Parameters:  
**tol** – the largest gap closed, a length.

Returns:  
this Face.

Examples

``` python
face.CloseGaps(1e-6)
```

Distance(*target: Point \| Point3 \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [EdgeView](#planex.EdgeView "planex.EdgeView") \| [VertexView](#planex.VertexView "planex.VertexView") \| [FaceView](#planex.FaceView "planex.FaceView") \| TopoDS_Shape \| np.ndarray*, */*, *project: bool = False*, *components: str \| None = None*, *signed: bool = False*) → float \| tuple\[float, ...\] \| np.ndarray  
The smallest distance to the target; 0 inside a face.

A target in another plane is measured in 3d, or projected into this plane with project.

Parameters:  
- **target** – a point, (h, v) in the plane or (x, y, z) in 3d, a Face, Shape, Wire, edge, vertex, face of a shape or OCC shape; many points as an (n, 2) or (n, 3) array.

- **project** – True projects a target in another plane into this one.

- **components** – letters of ‘hvxyz’: the components of the shortest connection from here to the target instead of its length.

- **signed** – True: the distance of points (h, v) to the boundary of the union of the faces (edges between faces do not count), negative inside, 0 on it.

Returns:  
a float; with components a tuple of them, one letter a float; many points an array (n,), with k components (n, k), one letter (n,).

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – it is empty; components has other letters; signed with components, with points not (h, v), or without faces.

- **TypeError** – the target has another form.

Examples

``` python
face.Distance((5, 0))
face.Distance(other, components="hv")
```

Measure(*name: str \| [FaceView](#planex.FaceView "planex.FaceView") \| [EdgeView](#planex.EdgeView "planex.EdgeView") \| None = None*, *to: str \| Point \| Point3 \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| None = None*, *project: bool = False*) → dict\
Measure(*f: Callable*, */*, *\*args*, *id: str \| None = None*, *\*\*params*) → object  
The measures of the faces and edges named name, or of the one with that id or selected, as a dict.

Its keys: type, faces, area, edges, length, center (in 3d; of an arc or circle its centre, with radius and angle), inertia, Ih, Iv, Ihv, I1, I2, principal_angle, bounding_box; with to also distance, du, dv, dx, dy, dz, points and the angle between two lines.

Parameters:  
- **name** – a name, an id, or a selected face or edge; None measures all.

- **to** – a name, or anything Distance takes: adds the distance to it.

- **project** – True projects a target of to in another plane into this one.

- **f** – a measurement, a callable f(obj, \*args, \*\*params) (see px.measurements): Measure returns its value.

- **args** – the further arguments of f.

- **id** – stores the measurement f under this id: obj.measures then holds it next to the standard measurements, RemoveMeasure(id) drops it.

- **params** – the keyword arguments of f.

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – no face or edge has that name or id.

- **TypeError** – name has another form.

- **TypeError** – id without a measurement f.

Examples

``` python
face.Measure()
face.Measure(px.measurements.MinThickness(), id="wall")
```

Offset(*d: float*, *inplace: bool = True*) → [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape")  
Grows the faces by d: the band of width [\|d\|](#id1) along their boundaries added for d \> 0, taken away for d \< 0.

The band is Wire.Offset of their edges, round around convex corners; the faces keep their properties, the new edges those of the edges they come from.

Parameters:  
- **d** – the width of the band, a length; d \> 0 grows, d \< 0 shrinks, 0 changes nothing.

- **inplace** – True changes this Face and returns it; False returns the offset as a new Shape and leaves this one.

Raises:  
**ValueError** – in place, the offset is several faces; inplace=False returns them as a Shape.

Examples

``` python
face.Offset(0.5)
band = face.Offset(0.5, inplace=False)
```

Plot(*\*args*, *\*\*kwargs*)  
Draws a planex object in its plane with matplotlib or plotly.

A sketch is drawn as sk.Plot draws it (show_constraints, show_ends, show_direction, show_parent); the other options are for the other objects, e.g. px.Plot(sk.Shape(), face_col=”C0”). An OCC shape is cut at the plane (px.Intersect3d(plane, shape)), or without one drawn flat in its own plane as px.FromOCC gives it. Fields: px.PlotField; meshes: px.PlotMesh.

Parameters:  
- **obj** – a Face, Shape, Wire, Compound, sketch, selection, DeformableShape or OCC shape, or an id that names one (“Sketch.1”, “Shape.2.Line.3”).

- **plane** – the plane that cuts an OCC shape; None draws it flat in its own plane.

- **ax** – a matplotlib Axes or a plotly Figure to draw into, which also selects the backend.

- **line_col** – the colour of every edge; “type” draws lines in black, arcs in arc_col and splines in spline_col, with a legend entry each; “property” takes each edge’s own col where it has one.

- **arc_col** – the colour of arcs with line_col=”type”.

- **spline_col** – the colour of splines with line_col=”type”.

- **face_col** – fills the closed loops (faces and shapes; a wire on its own stays an outline unless face_col is given); a fill other than the default gets a legend entry labelled with the object’s id (‘Face.3’), the default fill none; None draws the outlines only.

- **mark_edges_smaller** – marks the edges shorter than this at their midpoints.

- **mark_free_edges** – True marks the edges with an end no other edge shares.

- **highlight** – marks the edges given: ids (“Line.3”, “Shape.1.Line.3”), selected edges or faces (a face: its edges), a selection, or indices or a boolean mask over obj.edges (for a Compound those of its parts in turn).

- **legend** – True shows the legend.

- **show_constraints** – for a sketch, as sk.Plot.

- **show_ends** – for a sketch, as sk.Plot.

- **show_direction** – for a sketch, as sk.Plot.

- **show_parent** – for a sketch, as sk.Plot.

- **backend** – “matplotlib” or “plotly” without ax; None is matplotlib.

Returns:  
the matplotlib Axes or the plotly Figure.

Raises:  
**ValueError** – a sketch with an option for other objects, an option for sketches with another object, a plane with a planex object, obj is a plane, or backend is unknown.

Examples

``` python
px.Plot(face, line_col="type")
px.Plot(solid, px.XY)
```

Plot3d(*\*args*, *\*\*kwargs*)  
Draws planex objects, planes and OCC shapes in one 3d view.

Everything is exported to OCC, put into one compound and drawn; a sketch contributes its drawn edges. A plane is drawn as a square of side plane_size with a line along its u axis. backend “webgpu” draws with ngsolve_webgpu.jupyter.Draw: it needs ngsolve_webgpu (pip install ngsolve_webgpu, which brings the full ngsolve) and a browser with WebGPU, with the kernel on the same machine as the browser or its websocket port forwarded. backend “webgui” draws with netgen.webgui.Draw and needs only netgen.

Parameters:  
- **objects** – a Wire, Face, Shape, Compound, sketch, Plane or OCC shape, or a list of them.

- **plane_size** – the side of a plane’s square; None takes the largest extent of everything else, 1 without.

- **backend** – ‘webgpu’ or ‘webgui’.

- **kwargs** – go to the backend’s Draw (width, height; settings, euler_angles only for webgui).

Returns:  
the backend’s scene.

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – backend is unknown, or there is nothing to draw.

- **ImportError** – backend ‘webgpu’ without ngsolve_webgpu installed.

Examples

``` python
px.Plot3d([face, px.XY], plane_size=2)
shape.Plot3d(backend="webgui", height=400)
```

Polylines(*tol: float*) → list\[np.ndarray\]  
The loops and open chains as (n, 2) arrays of plane coordinates, each chord within tol of its edge.

A face gives its outer loop counterclockwise, then its holes clockwise; a shape its faces in turn, then its free wires; a wire’s loop runs the way the wire’s first edge runs; a closed loop ends at its first point.

Parameters:  
**tol** – the largest distance of a chord from its edge, a length \> 0.

Raises:  
**ValueError** – tol is not positive and finite, or below the rounding of an arc’s or a spline’s coordinates.

Examples

``` python
face.Polylines(0.01)
```

Simplified(*fit_splines: bool \| dict \| None = None*, *remove_edges_smaller: float \| None = None*, *close_gaps_smaller: float \| None = None*, *remove_free_edges: bool \| None = None*, *merge_collinear_closer: float \| None = None*, *remove_faces_smaller: float \| None = None*, *merge_small_faces_instead: bool \| None = None*, *fit_arcs: bool \| dict \| None = None*) → [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face")  
A copy defeatured as Simplify does it; this face is not changed.

Parameters:  
- **fit_splines** – fits splines to chains of short edges: True, False or a dict of the fit’s options (tol, max_edge_length, max_edge_angle, ignore_edges_smaller); None takes px.config.fit_splines.

- **remove_edges_smaller** – removes lines and arcs no longer than this; None takes px.config.remove_edges_smaller.

- **close_gaps_smaller** – closes gaps between ends up to this; None takes px.config.close_gaps_smaller.

- **remove_free_edges** – removes the edges that touch no other edge at either end; None takes px.config.remove_free_edges. In a Shape only the edges of its faces go, its wires stay (a wire of one isolated edge too).

- **merge_collinear_closer** – merges two lines whose common vertex is this close to the line through their far ends; None takes px.config.merge_collinear_closer.

- **remove_faces_smaller** – removes the faces of less area than this (0: none); None takes px.config.remove_faces_smaller.

- **merge_small_faces_instead** – True unites such a face with the face it shares the longest boundary with instead; None takes px.config.merge_small_faces_instead.

- **fit_arcs** – fits arcs to chains of short edges: True, False or a dict of FitArcs’ options; None takes px.config.fit_arcs.

Raises:  
**TypeError** – fit_splines or fit_arcs has another form or names an unknown option.

Examples


The face as an OCC face, or a compound if the export gives several, as ToOCCFace().

Parameters:  
- **fit_splines** – fits splines to chains of short edges: True, False or a dict of the fit’s options (tol, max_edge_length, max_edge_angle, ignore_edges_smaller); None takes px.config.fit_splines.

- **remove_edges_smaller** – removes lines and arcs no longer than this; None takes px.config.remove_edges_smaller.

- **close_gaps_smaller** – closes gaps between ends up to this; None takes px.config.close_gaps_smaller.

- **remove_free_edges** – removes the edges that touch no other edge at either end; None takes px.config.remove_free_edges. In a Shape only the edges of its faces go, its wires stay (a wire of one isolated edge too).

- **merge_collinear_closer** – merges two lines whose common vertex is this close to the line through their far ends; None takes px.config.merge_collinear_closer.

- **remove_faces_smaller** – removes the faces of less area than this (0: none); None takes px.config.remove_faces_smaller.

- **merge_small_faces_instead** – True unites such a face with the face it shares the longest boundary with instead; None takes px.config.merge_small_faces_instead.

- **fit_arcs** – fits arcs to chains of short edges: True, False or a dict of FitArcs’ options; None takes px.config.fit_arcs.

Raises:  
**TypeError** – fit_splines or fit_arcs has another form or names an unknown option.

Examples

``` python
face.ToOCCShape()
face.ToOCCShape(fit_arcs=True, remove_edges_smaller=1e-6)
```

- **remove_free_edges** – removes the edges that touch no other edge at either end; None takes px.config.remove_free_edges. In a Shape only the edges of its faces go, its wires stay (a wire of one isolated edge too).

- **merge_collinear_closer** – merges two lines whose common vertex is this close to the line through their far ends; None takes px.config.merge_collinear_closer.

- **remove_faces_smaller** – removes the faces of less area than this (0: none); None takes px.config.remove_faces_smaller.

- **merge_small_faces_instead** – True unites such a face with the face it shares the longest boundary with instead; None takes px.config.merge_small_faces_instead.

- **fit_arcs** – fits arcs to chains of short edges: True, False or a dict of FitArcs’ options; None takes px.config.fit_arcs.

Raises:

ToSVG(*\*args*, *\*\*kwargs*)  
The object as the text of an SVG picture in its plane coordinates, its faces filled.

A sketch is drawn in its own look: every element in the colour of its state (green fully constrained, black free, pink over-constrained) with its id when hovered, construction dashed, in a frame with numbered ticks on a grid.

Parameters:  
- **obj** – a Face, Shape, Wire, Compound, sketch or DeformableShape.

- **size** – the larger side of the picture in pixels.

- **options** – for a sketch: show_constraints=True adds a sign per constraint, show_ends=True a blue start and an orange end piece on every line and arc, show_direction=True an arrow from start to end; other objects ignore them.

Returns:  
the SVG text; None if the object has no extent.

Examples

``` python
face.ToSVG()
sk.ToSVG(size=500, show_constraints=True)
```

ToShapely(*\*args*, *\*\*kwargs*)  
Converts to a shapely geometry in plane coordinates, arcs and splines sampled within tol.

Faces that share an edge (a glued Shape) give a GeometryCollection of their polygons, since a MultiPolygon must not have parts sharing an edge.

Parameters:  
- **obj** – the Face, Shape, Wire, sketch (its Shape()) or Compound.

- **tol** – the largest distance of a chord from its arc or spline, a length. Where a face is thinner than tol its polygon is sampled again finer (to tol/1000), with a warning; still invalid, it is made valid (make_valid).

Returns:  
a Polygon or MultiPolygon for a Face, a Shape of faces or a sketch; a LineString or MultiLineString for a Wire or a Shape of wires; a GeometryCollection for a Compound or a Shape of both.

Examples

``` python
face.ToShapely()
px.ToShapely(shape, tol=1e-4)
```

Trim(*cutter: [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [EdgeView](#planex.EdgeView "planex.EdgeView") \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Sketch](sketches.md#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch") \| [QuickSketch](sketches.md#planex.QuickSketch "planex.QuickSketch") \| TopoDS_Shape*, *\**, *keep_closest_to: Point \| Point3 \| None = None*, *remove_closest_to: Point \| Point3 \| None = None*, *keep_largest: bool = False*, *keep_smallest: bool = False*, *keep_left: bool = False*, *keep_right: bool = False*) → [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape")  
Cuts every face and wire by the cutter and keeps the pieces the one option given chooses.

What the cutter does not separate stays as it is.

Parameters:  
- **cutter** – the edges that cut, a Wire, edge, Face, Shape, sketch or OCC shape; projected into the plane if it lies elsewhere.

- **keep_closest_to** – keeps the piece closest to this point (a face piece by its centre, a wire piece by itself), (h, v) or (x, y, z).

- **remove_closest_to** – removes the piece closest to this point and keeps the others.

- **keep_largest** – keeps the piece of the largest area (faces) or length (wires).

- **keep_smallest** – keeps the piece of the smallest area or length.

- **keep_left** – keeps the face pieces left of the cutter as drawn; a shape’s free wires stay.

- **keep_right** – keeps the face pieces right of the cutter as drawn; a shape’s free wires stay.

Returns:  
a new Shape; this one is not changed.

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – not exactly one option is given; keep_left or keep_right without faces, or no piece lies wholly on that side.

- **TypeError** – the cutter or the point has the wrong form.

Examples

``` python
face.Trim(px.Line((0, -5), (0, 5)), keep_left=True)
face.Trim(cutter, keep_closest_to=(2, 1))
```

WriteDXF(*\*args*, *\*\*kwargs*)  
Writes the edges as LINE, ARC and SPLINE entities of a DXF file, each edge once.

An edge’s name becomes its layer (the characters a layer name cannot have, such as / and :, become \_, with a warning), its col the true colour. The coordinates are divided by unit and \$INSUNITS names it.

Parameters:  
- **obj** – the Face, Shape, Wire, sketch or Compound to write.

- **path** – the file to write.

- **unit** – the length the file counts in (px.m, px.mm, px.inch, …).

Raises:  
- **TypeError** – unit is a name, not a length.

- **ValueError** – unit is not a positive finite length.

Examples

``` python
face.WriteDXF("part.dxf", unit=px.mm)
px.WriteDXF(shape, "part.dxf")
```

WriteGeo(*\*args*, *\*\*kwargs*)  
Writes the edges and faces as a gmsh .geo file.

Points carry the maxh of their edges and faces as the characteristic length; lines, circle arcs (split at half a circle) and splines as B-splines through planex’s approximation (not exact: .geo has no NURBS), every curve once; plane surfaces with their holes. Physical groups: a curve group per edge name, a surface group per face name, the unnamed edges and faces in a curve and a surface group named “unnamed” (gmsh writes only elements in a group once there is one, and netgen’s ReadGmsh needs every group named and the boundary segments). Periodic identifications become Periodic Curve.

Parameters:  
- **obj** – the Face, Shape, Wire, sketch or Compound to write.

- **path** – the file to write.

Examples

``` python
face.WriteGeo("part.geo")
px.WriteGeo(shape, "part.geo")
```

WriteStep(*\*args*, *\*\*kwargs*)

- **path** – the file to write.

- **options** – the options of obj.ToOCCShape (fit_splines, fit_arcs, remove_edges_smaller, …).

Distance(*target: Point \| Point3 \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [EdgeView](#planex.EdgeView "planex.EdgeView") \| [VertexView](#planex.VertexView "planex.VertexView") \| [FaceView](#planex.FaceView "planex.FaceView") \| TopoDS_Shape \| np.ndarray*, */*, *project: bool = False*, *components: str \| None = None*, *signed: bool = False*) → float \| tuple\[float, ...\] \| np.ndarray  
The smallest distance from the vertex to the target.

A target in another plane is measured in 3d, or projected into this plane with project.

Parameters:  
- **target** – a point, (h, v) in the plane or (x, y, z) in 3d, a Face, Shape, Wire, edge, vertex, face of a shape or OCC shape; many points as an (n, 2) or (n, 3) array.

- **project** – True projects a target in another plane into this one.

- **components** – letters of ‘hvxyz’: the components of the shortest connection from here to the target instead of its length.

- **signed** – only False: a vertex has no inside.

Returns:  
a float; with components a tuple of them, one letter a float; many points an array (n,), with k components (n, k), one letter (n,).

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – signed=True; components has other letters.

- **TypeError** – the target has another form.

Examples

``` python
vertex.Distance((5, 0))
vertex.Distance(other, components="hv")
```

# Files and other libraries

Reading and writing files, conversions to and from other Python libraries, and wires from arrays of points. See [Files](../core/files.md) for the guide.

FromPolyline(*points: np.ndarray \| list\[Point\]*, */*, *closed: bool = False*, *\**, *plane: [Plane](geometry.md#planex.Plane "planex.Plane") \| None = None*, *name: str \| None = None*, *maxh: float \| None = None*, *col: tuple\[float, ...\] \| None = None*, *minh: float \| None = None*, *hpref: float \| None = None*, *layer: int \| None = None*, *partition: list\[float\] \| None = None*, *id: str \| None = None*) → [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire")  
A wire of lines through the points, the properties on every line.

Parameters:  
- **points** – an (n, 2) or (n, 3) array or a sequence of (h, v) or (x, y, z) on the plane; a point equal to the one before is skipped.

- **closed** – True joins the last point to the first; a last point equal to the first adds no line.

- **plane** – the plane the wire lies on: a Plane, netgen Axes, a sketch, Shape, Face, Wire, Compound or planar OCC shape (its plane); default the xy plane.

- **name** – the name of the lines.

- **maxh** – the largest mesh size on the lines (netgen’s maxh).

- **col** – the colour (r, g, b) or (r, g, b, a), each in 0..1.

- **minh** – the smallest mesh size on the lines (netgen’s minh).

- **hpref** – netgen’s hpref.

- **layer** – netgen’s layer number.

- **partition** – the mesh points along each line as increasing fractions of its length in (0, 1).

- **id** – the id of what it returns (of a list’s items id.1, id.2, …, of a dict’s id.key); default the kind that made it and a number, given when first asked for.

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – fewer than two different points; the lines cross, overlap or revisit a point (px.Wires of the lines cuts them into clean wires); a mesh size is not positive and finite.

- **TypeError** – plane has another form.

Examples

``` python
px.FromPolyline([(0, 0), (10, 0), (10, 5)])
px.FromPolyline([(0, 0), (10, 0), (10, 5)], closed=True, name="outline", maxh=0.5)
```

&nbsp;

FromDXF(*path: str \| os.PathLike*, */*, *tol: float = 1e-07*, *layers: list\[str\] \| None = None*, *unit: float \| None = None*, *plane: [Plane](geometry.md#planex.Plane "planex.Plane") \| None = None*, *\**, *id: str \| None = None*) → list\[[Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire")\]  
Reads the lines, arcs, circles, polylines, splines and ellipses of a DXF file’s model space as clean wires.

The coordinates are scaled to metres; the wires are built as by px.Wires: ends within tol (after scaling) joined, the edges cut against each other (crossings, T-junctions, an overlapping stretch kept once), then the chains. Blocks (INSERT) are read as their entities. The layer becomes the edges’ name, the colour their col; an ellipse becomes a spline through sampled points. px.Glue(wires) makes them one Shape.

Parameters:  
- **path** – the DXF file.

- **tol** – ends closer than this (after scaling) are joined, a length.

- **layers** – the names of the layers to read; None reads all.

- **unit** – the length the file counts in (px.mm, px.inch, …); None takes the unit its header (\$INSUNITS) names, metres with a warning if it names none.

- **plane** – the plane of the wires; None is the xy plane.

- **id** – the id of what it returns (of a list’s items id.1, id.2, …, of a dict’s id.key); default the kind that made it and a number, given when first asked for.

Returns:  
a list of wires; \[\] for an empty drawing.

Raises:  
**ValueError** – unit is not a positive length.

Examples

``` python
px.FromDXF("part.dxf", unit=px.mm)
px.Glue(px.FromDXF("part.dxf", layers=["outline"]))
```

&nbsp;

WriteDXF(*obj: [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [Sketch](sketches.md#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch") \| [QuickSketch](sketches.md#planex.QuickSketch "planex.QuickSketch") \| [Compound](geometry.md#planex.Compound "planex.Compound")*, *path: str \| os.PathLike*, */*, *unit: float = 1.0*) → None  
Writes the edges as LINE, ARC and SPLINE entities of a DXF file, each edge once.

An edge’s name becomes its layer (the characters a layer name cannot have, such as / and :, become \_, with a warning), its col the true colour. The coordinates are divided by unit and \$INSUNITS names it.

Parameters:  
- **obj** – the Face, Shape, Wire, sketch or Compound to write.

- **path** – the file to write.

- **unit** – the length the file counts in (px.m, px.mm, px.inch, …).

Raises:  
- **TypeError** – unit is a name, not a length.

- **ValueError** – unit is not a positive finite length.

Examples

``` python
face.WriteDXF("part.dxf", unit=px.mm)
px.WriteDXF(shape, "part.dxf")
```

&nbsp;

FromOCC(*source: Any*, */*, *\**, *id: str \| None = None*) → [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape")  
Reads a planar OCC shape, or a STEP, BREP or IGES file of one, as a Shape on its plane.

Files are read by netgen, which keeps the names. The faces come with their properties, glued as by px.Glue (an overlap becomes a face of its own); edges on no face become wires; every edge keeps its properties. px.Intersect3d(plane, shape) gives a section of a shape that is not planar, px.Project(shape, plane) a projection.

Parameters:  
- **source** – an OCC shape, or the path of a STEP, BREP or IGES file.

- **id** – the id of what it returns (of a list’s items id.1, id.2, …, of a dict’s id.key); default the kind that made it and a number, given when first asked for.

Raises:  
**ValueError** – the shape does not lie in one plane, or it has no edges.

Examples

``` python
px.FromOCC("bracket.step")
px.FromOCC(occ_face)
```

WriteStep(*obj: [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [Sketch](sketches.md#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch") \| [QuickSketch](sketches.md#planex.QuickSketch "planex.QuickSketch") \| [Compound](geometry.md#planex.Compound "planex.Compound")*, *path: str \| os.PathLike*, */*, *\*\*options: Any*) → None  
Writes the OCC export (obj.ToOCCShape) as a STEP file.

- **path** – the file to write.

- **options** – the options of obj.ToOCCShape (fit_splines, fit_arcs, remove_edges_smaller, …).

Examples

``` python
face.WriteStep("part.step")
px.WriteStep(shape, "part.step", fit_arcs=True)
```

&nbsp;

WriteGeo(*obj: [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [Sketch](sketches.md#planex.Sketch "planex.Sketch") \| [QuickSketch](sketches.md#planex.QuickSketch "planex.QuickSketch") \| [Compound](geometry.md#planex.Compound "planex.Compound")*, *path: str \| os.PathLike*, */*) → None  
Writes the edges and faces as a gmsh .geo file.

Points carry the maxh of their edges and faces as the characteristic length; lines, circle arcs (split at half a circle) and splines as B-splines through planex’s approximation (not exact: .geo has no NURBS), every curve once; plane surfaces with their holes. Physical groups: a curve group per edge name, a surface group per face name, the unnamed edges and faces in a curve and a surface group named “unnamed” (gmsh writes only elements in a group once there is one, and netgen’s ReadGmsh needs every group named and the boundary segments). Periodic identifications become Periodic Curve.

Parameters:  
- **obj** – the Face, Shape, Wire, sketch or Compound to write.

- **path** – the file to write.

Examples

``` python
face.WriteGeo("part.geo")
px.WriteGeo(shape, "part.geo")
```

&nbsp;

FromKiCad(*path: str \| os.PathLike*, */*, *layer: str \| list\[float\] \| dict \| Any \| None = None*, *remove_faces_smaller: float \| None = 5e-08*, *merge_small_faces_instead: bool \| None = True*, *remove_edges_smaller: float \| None = None*, *close_gaps_smaller: float \| None = None*, *remove_free_edges: bool \| None = None*, *merge_collinear_closer: float \| None = None*, *\**, *id: str \| None = None*) → dict\[str, [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape")\] \| [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| Any  
Reads a KiCad board (.kicad_pcb, KiCad 9 and later) in metres, y up: its layers as Shapes, or the board in 3d.

A board of another program (Altium, Eagle, PADS, CADSTAR, Fabmaster, P-CAD, SolidWorks PCB: a file that is no .kicad_pcb) is converted first with KiCad 10’s kicad-cli (pcb import), found as \$PLANEX_KICAD_CLI, on the PATH or where KiCad installs it.

A copper layer is every track, arc, via, pad, filled zone and copper drawing on it, united per net with the faces named by the net; the drill holes through it are cut out, the edges of plated holes (vias and plated pads) named “pth”, of unplated ones “npth”. The outline face is named “profile”, the holes through the whole board are cut out of it. Every other layer is what KiCad prints there: lines, arcs and Bezier curves (as exact splines) as wide as drawn (dashed ones solid), filled shapes and zones as regions, the drawings of footprints too. The solder mask and paste layers are their openings: the pads on them grown by their solder mask or paste margin (the pad’s, else the footprint’s, else the board’s setup) as the file’s KiCad plots them (a round rectangle keeps its corner ratio in a KiCad 9 file, grows exactly in a KiCad 10 one), what is drawn there, the vias the board’s (or the via’s own) tenting leaves open and the tracks and copper drawings marked for an opening; with the setup’s solder mask minimum width, openings closer than it are joined as KiCad joins them. Text, dimensions, tables, barcodes and hatched fills are left out, with one warning giving their counts; zones need to be filled in KiCad (a warning says when they are not). Copper and drill holes are coloured gold (col), the board solder mask green, in 2d and in 3d. Files newer than the newest tested (KiCad 10, version 20260206) warn.

In 3d every dielectric is the outline extruded between its two copper layers (solids named dielectric_1, … from the top), drilled where a hole joins both, so the hole walls are faces named “pth” or “npth”; the copper layers are faces at their heights (B.Cu at z = 0), named by net.

The cleanup options are those of the OCC exports (ToOCCShape): the copper layers and the outline are cleaned with them (Simplify), the other layers keep what KiCad prints, the 3d board is exported with them.

Parameters:  
- **path** – the board file.

- **layer** – None: a dict {KiCad layer name: Shape}: the copper layers from the top (F.Cu, In1.Cu, …, B.Cu), each even when empty, then the board outline “Edge.Cuts”, then every other layer of the board’s layer table that holds something, in the table’s order. A layer name (“F.Cu”, “F.SilkS”, …): that layer’s Shape alone. A stackup: the board in 3d as one glued OCC shape: a list of dielectric thicknesses in millimetres from the top, as the manufacturer gives it (e.g. \[0.2, 1.3, 0.2\] for four copper layers), a stackup of px.stackups (a dict {number of copper layers: such a list}, e.g. px.stackups.jlc7628), or px.stackups.kicad (the stackup in the board file).

- **remove_faces_smaller** – faces of less area than this (m^2) are united with the neighbour they share the longest edge with, such as the slivers a zone fill’s polygon leaves next to an exact drill circle (merged, the hole keeps its exact circle); None takes px.config.remove_faces_smaller.

- **merge_small_faces_instead** – False throws such faces away instead; None takes px.config.merge_small_faces_instead.

- **remove_edges_smaller** – removes lines and arcs no longer than this; None takes px.config.remove_edges_smaller.

- **close_gaps_smaller** – closes gaps between ends up to this; None takes px.config.close_gaps_smaller.

- **remove_free_edges** – removes the edges that touch no other edge at either end; None takes px.config.remove_free_edges.

- **merge_collinear_closer** – merges two lines whose common vertex is this close to the line through their far ends; None takes px.config.merge_collinear_closer.

- **id** – the id of what it returns (of a list’s items id.1, id.2, …, of a dict’s id.key); default the kind that made it and a number, given when first asked for.

Returns:  
a dict of Shapes; a layer name: a Shape; a stackup: a netgen.occ shape.

Return type:  
layer None

Raises:  
- **ValueError** – a legacy board (before KiCad 6) or a file older than KiCad 9 (version 20241229): open and save it in KiCad 9 or later; kicad-cli could not convert the board; a layer name the board’s layer table does not have; a stackup without an entry for the board’s number of copper layers, with another number of thicknesses than copper layers - 1, or with a thickness not positive; px.stackups.kicad and the file has no stackup or one that does not fit; the board has no outline on Edge.Cuts where one is needed.

- **RuntimeError** – a board of another program and no kicad-cli of KiCad 10 or later can be run.

Examples

``` python
px.FromKiCad("board.kicad_pcb", layer="F.Cu")
px.FromKiCad("board.kicad_pcb", layer=px.stackups.jlc7628)
```

&nbsp;

WriteKiCad(*path: str \| os.PathLike*, *layers: dict\[str, [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [Compound](geometry.md#planex.Compound "planex.Compound")\] \| list\[[Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Compound](geometry.md#planex.Compound "planex.Compound")\]*, */*, *outline: [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [Compound](geometry.md#planex.Compound "planex.Compound") \| None = None*, *unit: float = 1.0*, *pth: [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [Compound](geometry.md#planex.Compound "planex.Compound") \| None = None*, *npth: [Shape](geometry.md#planex.Shape "planex.Shape") \| [Face](geometry.md#planex.Face "planex.Face") \| [Wire](geometry.md#planex.Wire "planex.Wire") \| [Compound](geometry.md#planex.Compound "planex.Compound") \| None = None*, *tol: float = 1e-06*, *thickness: float = 0.0016*, *line_width: float = 0.0001*) → None  
Writes the layers as a KiCad 9 board (.kicad_pcb, millimetres, y down).

The board has as many copper layers as the highest one given needs, those not given empty. Everything lies in one plane, the xy plane or the plane of the first shape. Every face becomes one filled polygon (gr_poly): lines and arcs exactly, splines as lines within tol, a face with holes as one outline with every hole joined to it by a bridge there and back, as KiCad fractures a zone. Edges on no face become lines of line_width (gr_line, gr_arc), except on copper, which needs an area: they are left out with a warning. The outline’s loops become lines, arcs and circles on Edge.Cuts.

Drill holes are the faces of pth and npth (or of layers\[“pth”\] and layers\[“npth”\]) and the holes of the layers’ faces whose edges are all named “pth” or “npth” (as FromKiCad names them). Every hole is cut out of every copper layer and the outline. A round plated hole becomes a via through all copper layers, its pad as wide as the copper around the hole on the layer with the least (it adds no copper). A round unplated hole becomes a footprint “MountingHole” with one unplated pad. Other holes become cutouts of the outline.

Nets: faces on one layer with one name, and faces a plated hole goes through, are one net, named after the first named face from the top layer down (faces with two names warn), else net1, net2, … from the top. Numbers are written in millimetres with 6 decimals; the uuids are made from each element’s text, so the same layers give the same file.

Parameters:  
- **path** – the file to write.

- **layers** – a dict {KiCad layer name: Shape, Face, Wire or Compound} (copper “F.Cu”, “In1.Cu”, …, “B.Cu”, the board outline “Edge.Cuts”, the other KiCad layers such as “F.SilkS” or “F.Mask”, and “pth”, “npth”), or a list of the copper layers from the top.

- **outline** – the board outline, instead of “Edge.Cuts” in the dict.

- **unit** – the length the geometry counts in (px.m, px.mm, …); tol, thickness and line_width count in it too.

- **pth** – the plated holes, as faces or closed wires.

- **npth** – the unplated holes, as faces or closed wires.

- **tol** – the largest distance of the lines from a spline.

- **thickness** – the board’s thickness.

- **line_width** – the width of the lines of edges on no face.

Raises:  
**ValueError** – unit, tol, thickness or line_width is not a positive length; the outline or a kind of holes is given twice; a name is no KiCad layer; more than 32 copper layers; the layers lie in different planes; an open wire as a hole; a plated hole without copper around it on a copper layer.

Examples

``` python
px.WriteKiCad("board.kicad_pcb", {"F.Cu": top, "B.Cu": bottom}, outline=board, unit=px.mm)
px.WriteKiCad("board.kicad_pcb", [top, bottom], pth=vias)
```
